name: Vertica
tagline: Veteran MPP columnar analytics database from the C-Store lineage, now owned by Rocket Software.
description: Vertica is a column-store MPP database that grew out of Michael Stonebraker's C-Store research in 2005, passing through HP, Micro Focus and OpenText before Rocket Software bought it in May 2026. It stores data as sorted, encoded projections and runs either in Enterprise mode on local disks or Eon mode with storage on S3-compatible object stores and elastic subclusters. Built-in time-series, geospatial, in-database ML, Kafka ingestion and querying of external Parquet make it a capable all-rounder for large on-prem or hybrid estates. Licensing cost and yet another ownership change are the main concerns.
statusNote: OpenText sold Vertica to Rocket Software (a Bain Capital company); the deal closed 11 May 2026.

license.name: Proprietary (free Community Edition up to 1 TB)

pricing.notes: Licensed by raw data volume or subscription; a free Community Edition is limited to 3 nodes and 1 TB.

scale.notes: Shared-nothing Enterprise mode or Eon mode with subclusters over object storage; multi-PB deployments documented.

strengths: Mature columnar MPP engine with aggressive encoding and compression
Eon mode separates compute and storage with elastic subclusters
Built-in time-series gap filling, geospatial and in-database ML
Native Kafka ingestion and external Parquet/ORC tables
Runs on-prem, in any cloud or on Kubernetes
weaknesses: Expensive licensing based on data volume
Repeated ownership changes (HP, Micro Focus, OpenText, Rocket) create roadmap risk
Projection design and tuning require specialist skills
useCases: Large on-prem or hybrid enterprise warehouses
notIdealFor: Small teams wanting a serverless SaaS
